newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schloendorff quits post at Babelsburg studios.
newsitem.headline: Schloendorff quits post at Babelsburg studios.

text.p: Germany's Babelsburg Film Studios said on Friday film director Volker Schloendorff, whose films include Oscar-winner "The Tin Drum", was leaving his post as the studios' managing director.

Although Schloendorff will stay on as a member the board of the studios' new holding company, a Babelsburg spokesman said the director will hand over the management of the studios' day-to-day activities to Friedrich-Carl Wachs on October 1.
"Mr Schloendorff will be active on the holding company's board for another five years and stay on in an advisory capacity for production development," spokesman Juergen Schepers said.
Details about the organisation and activities of the holding will be announced on September 3, he added.

Babelsburg served as the birthplace of German cinema, where the young Marlene Dietrich starred in some of her most glamourous film roles in the 1920s and Joseph Goebbels later churned out Nazi propaganda pictures.

Schloendorff saw the studios through their five-year privatisation, which began in 1992 when the French industrial group Compagnie Generale des Eaux's bought former communist East Germany's Defa studios.

Schepers said Schloendorff was concerned that the studios were not drawing more big-budget film productions, despite its much-improved technical facilities and that TV series and game shows still represented three-quarters of productions there.
Schepers said Schloendorff predicted the studios would need another three years before its could establish itself as a powerful draw for European and U.S. filmmakers.
Schloendorff's successor, Wachs, was previously responsible for audio-visual media at the Bauer Verlag publishing house in Hamburg, Schepers said.
